title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation system was used to create non-consensual intimate imagery of a real person without her knowledge or consent. The person who operated the system obtained source photographs from the victim's private social media accounts and then distributed the generated images across multiple platforms using anonymous accounts to avoid detection.

What enabled this harm was the absence of any deployed safeguard in the AI system itself. The image generator had no mechanism to prevent the creation of explicit imagery of real, named individuals. No human review occurred before distribution because the attacker bypassed platform moderation by using fake accounts and multiple services.

Whether the AI system's developers provided any technical measures to block non-consensual intimate imagery creation, such as facial recognition or user warnings, is not established from the reporting. The case shows a known risk of image generation tools used in isolation from other protections: they can be repurposed for harassment when no safety layer exists between the user's intent and the system's output.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and sharing artificial intelligence-generated obscene images of a college acquaintance. The suspect, a bachelor's degree graduate in Electronics and Communication Engineering from East Punjabi Bagh, obtained photographs from the woman's private social media accounts and used AI technology to create fake explicit images. He then distributed this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The case began when the 22-year-old female victim reported to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi that unknown individuals were circulating morphed photographs and videos of her with threatening messages intended to harass and humiliate her. Police formed a team to trace the digital evidence and fake profiles. During interrogation, Bansal admitted he knew the victim from college and had developed personal resentment toward her following repeated conflicts. He disclosed that after initially uploading the content, other online users created additional explicit images that he then reshared. Investigators recovered a mobile phone, two SIM cards, and other digital evidence from the suspect, with further investigation ongoing.
